title: Multi-GPU steady-state variance profiler for sustained tokens/sec and p95 regression detection
creator: Ayesha Raman
description: Build an end-to-end profiling harness that measures sustained tokens/sec and p95 tail latency variability across multi-GPU tensor+pipeline parallel configurations. This ticket focuses on steady-state variance (not cold-start bursts) and introduces automated regression detection that flags sustained drops in throughput or increases in p95 over configurable windows. The goal is to detect subtle regressions introduced by kernel changes, batching adjustments, or KV cache heuristics before they hit production workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can run reproducible steady-state runs for TP/PP mixes (examples: TP=2/PP=2, TP=4/PP=1) and export a 1-minute sliding-window timeseries of tokens/sec and p95 at 1s granularity.
2) Baseline profiling suite runnable via ci/bench/mgpu-stable.sh and stores results in the benchmarking S3 bucket with metadata tags (model, seq_len, batch, TP, PP, image).
3) Regression detector alerts if sustained tokens/sec delta > 5% for >= 10 minutes or p95 increase > 10% for >= 10 minutes. Alerts must include reproducible command, config, and link to raw traces.
4) Documentation added to Confluence with how to interpret variance reports and how to re-run failed cases locally.
5) End-to-end PR with unit tests for the detector logic and an integration run recorded in the perf dashboard.
test_plan:
- Create canonical configs for 2 models: small GPT-like (8B) and medium transformer (30B) using quantized kernels.
- Run three stability scenarios: (A) steady full-load for 60m, (B) warmup + steady for 30m, (C) intermittent microbursts for 20m.
- Collect metrics: tokens/sec (1s), p50/p95 latency per token (1s buckets), GPU util, PCIe bandwidth, KV cache hit rate.
- Inject synthetic regressor in kernel selector (feature-flagged) to validate detector alerts.
- Validate results against historical baselines stored in perf-dashboard (compare median and tail).
steps: 1) Add a new harness script ci/bench/mgpu-stable.sh that composes cluster topology and runtime flags for TP/PP.
2) Extend our telemetry exporter to emit 1s-sampled tokens/sec and p95 as metrics to the perf-metrics ingestion endpoint.
3) Implement regression-detector service module (bench/regdetector) with configurable windows and thresholds and unit tests.
4) Create CI job perf:mgpu-stable that runs a 30m smoke and uploads artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/mgpu-stable/{date}/{run-id}.
5) Wire alerting to the perf-dashboard with links back to raw traces and the exact harness command used.
6) Author Confluence doc: 'MGPU steady-state variance profiler' with runbook and how to triage alerts.
7) Run full 60m canonical runs for both models and record baselines in runtime-1.20 branch before merging.
8) Obtain sign-off from runtime-qa and PM and schedule a dry-run with Dedicated infra team to validate on reserved pools.
9) Roll out the detector behind a feature flag and monitor for 7 days before enabling automatic incident pages.
10) Follow-up: add automated nightly comparisons to highlight regressions vs last successful baseline.
metrics: steady_tokens_per_sec: target > 600000 (for 4xA100 baseline, seq_len=1024, batch_per_device tuned)
p95_per_token: target < 150ms for generation segment (measured as per-token tail latency)
throughput_variance: < 8% coeff of variation over 30m steady window
regression_sensitivity: detect >=5% sustained delta over 10m window

notes: Avoid conflating warmup variance with steady-state: harness will have a mandatory warmup segment that is excluded from regression windows. Detector will be conservative by default (alerts noisy otherwise). Also include an 'explain' dump that prints kernel selection, batch sizes, and cache hit rate for any window that triggers an alert. Document how to reproduce on local devbox with subset topology (2 GPUs).
